title: Review stream: S<->K integration contract
description:
**Review stream for Stuart — one review, one test pass, 20 tickets.**

## The one test pass — run from Platform S against Platform K

The acceptance here is an S-side behaviour, so this is the only stream whose pass the K-side author cannot run alone:

register-connector -> originate carrying `identityCommitment` -> anchor -> verify -> read anchor status -> erasure by `external_ref` -> rotate and bulk re-key -> confirm revoke-on-rotate.

Plus the K-side `systemTest` **Integration mode** that KS-608 already names (`GET /api/anchors/{id}` and verify must not contradict each other).

## Why these twenty

Seventeen come from the *Integrate S with K* project. Three come from *Anchoring & Chain Integrity* — **KS-721** (platform-s's opaque identityCommitment), **KS-683** (a consumer repolling anchors K reports as terminally failed) and **KS-735** (what verify shows the user after a rename). Their acceptance is only observable from S, so they test here rather than with the K-side chain tickets.

**Answer from S, read at S develop `a77652e`, which dev-ps runs: yes, S handles a null `blockHeight`. Nothing more is owed from S for PR 2054 / KS-1509.**

* Every read of `blockchain.blockHeight` goes through `FlexibleInt64Converter` (`ssd/Services/CardanoAnchor/FlexibleInt64Converter.cs`) into a `long?`. JSON `null`, a missing key, an empty string and any unreadable value all become `null`, and the rest of the payload is kept (PS-647). `FlexibleInt64ConverterTests` has a `{"blockHeight":null}` case.
* S does no arithmetic on it:
  * the refresher writes `AnchorBlockHeight` only when the value is not null (`CardanoAnchorRefresher.cs:1081`);
  * the admin anchor pages print `—` for a missing block (`Index.cshtml:244`, `Details.cshtml:144`, `Chain.cshtml:210`), so a 0 becoming null there is the improvement you describe;
  * the Verify page shows the block row only when it has a value (`_VerifyResult.cshtml:585`).
* On `anchored` for a pending document (KS-2096): S's document read derives its state from `status` and the transaction hash, not from that flag (PS-1429, `CardanoAnchorService.cs:1462`). Verify adds "not yet confirmed" when the chain has not confirmed (`VerifyHeadline.ChainUnconfirmed`).
* **Not read live:** k25 is on kintsugi since 8 Nov 20:16 UTC, and dev-ps has written no anchor since 6 Nov. The next dev-ps upload will show it.

Your snapshot predates S's August changes, as you suspected; the lines above are from the current code.

When it ships, the block height of a pending document reads `null` instead of `0` on three route families of the originate service. In the Platform S code that could be read, one page changes (the admin `Block #` column: 0 becomes a dash) and the verify page does not. One question for Stuart's team is at the end: does the deployed Platform S handle a null `blockHeight` on that field? No answer is needed before the merge. What changes in Platform K (PR head `7bd7697c86ad`, read from the code):
* `blockchain.blockHeight` reads `null`, not `0`, for a pending document on GET `/api/documents/:id`, on the 202 answer of POST `/api/documents/:id/anchor`, and on the verify answers (POST `/api/verification/verify`, the file verify and the v2 verify list). The key stays. Rows already stored with `0` keep it; there is no migration.
* `anchored` on GET `/api/documents/:id` is still `true` for a pending document. This PR does not touch that.

What this means for Platform S, as read from a snapshot of its code:
* The admin anchor pages' `Block #` column (`Views/CardanoAnchorAdmin/Details.cshtml` line 99, `Index.cshtml` line 204, fed by `CardanoAnchorService.cs` line 458) reads 0 for these documents today and would read a dash. That page was wrong before and is better after.
* The verify page does not change. Its "Blockchain anchor" card shows only when `Anchored` or a transaction hash is present (`_VerifyResult.cshtml` line 76); these documents have neither, so the card is absent now and after.
* KS-1333 (PR 1500, merged 2026-10-12, commit `037575399cba`) is the earlier change that already moved a document with a hash and no height from Block 0 to no Block row on that page. Its commit message, as the review of PR 2054 read it, says the external reader was unverified.
* For a pending document that page says "Document verified ... anchored on the blockchain" (`_VerifyResult.cshtml` line 27). Platform K sets that state when anchoring is accepted, before the chain confirms, and did so on purpose (KS-563). PR 2054 does not change it.

Limits: every Platform S line above was read, not run. It comes from a snapshot of Platform S dated about June (newest file 2026-06-16), read by the review of PR 2054; the C# was not executed and nothing was tried against a running Platform S. The deployed Platform S has moved since: the snapshot has no `onBehalfOf`, which Platform K's anchoring code says Platform S has sent since 2026-08-21 (PS-616). So none of the above says what the deployed Platform S does.

Question: does the deployed Platform S handle a null `blockHeight` on that field, meaning it reads `blockHeight` nowhere beyond the two places above and does no arithmetic on it? If so, nothing more is owed from your side.
